sentences.text: Chubutinectes is an extinct genus of elasmosaurid plesiosaur known from the Late Cretaceous La Colonia Formation in Argentina.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — includes disarticulated vertebrae, ribs, girdles, limb elements, and roughly three hundred and fifty stomach stones.
Parts of the skull and the front neck bones were likely washed away by erosion before the fossil was found.
This immature individual had a 1.4-meter-long dorsal region, suggesting it would have been larger than an adult Kawanectes.
The holotype specimen of Chubutinectes was discovered in 2009 on the Somún Curá plateau in Chubut Province, Argentina.
Chubutinectes carmeloi was described as a new genus and species in 2023 by O'Gorman and colleagues.
The genus name Chubutinectes combines the name of the province Chubut with the Greek word for swimmer.
The species name carmeloi honors Carmelo Muñoz, who discovered the holotype.
The presence of gastroliths in the fossil record indicates Chubutinectes likely swallowed stones to aid digestion.
Chubutinectes is classified within the family Elasmosauridae.
Chubutinectes lived during the upper Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous.
Fossil evidence suggests Chubutinectes lived less than 67.3 million years ago.
Unlike the estuarine-dwelling Kawanectes, Chubutinectes lived in marine environments.
Chubutinectes inhabited warm, relatively shallow neritic marine waters.
The time range for Chubutinectes is estimated between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
